claims.claim: Doctorow argues that prompting a model for a rebuttal yields a blob of plausible sentences that is just stochastic word-salad until a human who understands the issue verifies it line by line.
claims.source: Cory Doctorow, novelist and journalist, Pluralistic, 2 March 2026
claims.quote: you have generated a blob of plausible sentences
claims.page: para. beginning "You haven't generated a rebuttal"

claims.claim: Doctorow describes what a chatbot costlessly produces as infinite volumes of verbose, plausible-seeming topical sentences.
claims.source: Cory Doctorow, novelist and journalist, Pluralistic, 2 March 2026
claims.quote: infinite volumes of verbose, plausible-seeming topical sentences
claims.page: para. beginning "Remember: even the AI companies will tell you"

claims.claim: Mark Williams rejects the premise of AI-spotting, arguing that machine writing does not carry a stable, visible fingerprint.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: machine writing carries a stable, visible fingerprint

claims.claim: Williams argues that what the supposed AI tells actually mark is the fingerprint of editing - clarity, structure, transitions, a point that goes somewhere - which is a feature of good writing whoever produced the first draft.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: What it carries is the fingerprint of editing

claims.claim: Williams argues that classifiers cannot reliably separate AI prose from human prose because the models were trained on human prose, so the categories overlap by construction.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.page: section beginning "So here's the actual argument"

claims.claim: Williams argues that detectors falsely flag non-native English writing because ESL prose tends toward simpler sentence-length variance, safer phrasing and fewer idioms, the very features detectors treat as tells.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: simpler sentence-length variance, safer phrasing, fewer idioms
claims.page: section beginning "So here's the actual argument"

claims.claim: Williams discloses that the twenty satirical tell-tale signs in his own piece were not written by him but gathered from several AI models, whose sharpest lines he picked and presented as one voice.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: I put a version of this challenge to several AI models

claims.claim: Strauss reports that the AI-driven author scams she tracks are marked by hyper-personalization coupled with lavish praise, which she attributes to generative AI.
claims.page: para. beginning "The one thing the scammers haven't changed"

claims.claim: Strauss reports that receiving multiple flattering yet suspiciously similar solicitations every day is itself what makes the AI-written approaches start to seem inauthentic.
claims.page: para. beginning "The one thing the scammers haven't changed"

claims.claim: Strauss identifies friendly, open-ended inquiry as a common ingredient of AI marketing solicitations, used to incentivize a reply and draw the writer into a long exchange.
claims.quote: friendly, open-ended inquiry is a common ingredient

claims.claim: In a pre-registered study of 81 participants post-editing LLM drafts for personal writing tasks, the post-edited text still remained stylistically closer to LLM text than to the participants' own unassisted control text.
claims.source: Baumler, Bao, Nghiem, Yang, Carpuat and Daume III, University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: post-edited text still remains stylistically closer in style to LLM text

claims.claim: The same study measured post-edited writing as significantly more stylistically homogeneous than unassisted writing, at p = .0002 with Hedges g = 1.42 and a 95% CI of [1.33, 1.51].
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: post-edited writing is indeed more stylistically homogeneous than unassisted writing

claims.feature: other: which features survive human editing
claims.claim: The same study found participants' post-edited text significantly more stylistically similar to other participants' post-edited text than to their own control writing, showing that some features of the LLM stylistic fingerprint are consistently preserved after post-editing across different participants.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: are consistently preserved after post-editing across different participants

claims.feature: other: which features survive human editing
claims.claim: The study concludes that the human-like changes made during post-editing are meaningfully unique to individuals while the AI-like aspects that are not addressed during post-editing are meaningfully shared between participants.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: the AI-like aspects that are not addressed during post-editing

claims.claim: In the study's qualitative coding, some participant edits removed words or punctuation commonly associated with LLM-generated text, the examples given being em dashes and the word dive, while others added contractions.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: some edits removed words or punctuation commonly associated with LLM-generated text
